title: exposure-rhythm-and-human-gates-scratchpad
body:
Purpose
---
This doc is a working sketch for a cadence-first canary + A/B framework that centers human decision points (gates) on a calendar rhythm rather than purely on metric streaming. Goal: reduce the cognitive load of cross-functional launches by creating short, repeatable rituals that align eng, product, SRE, and safety.

Scope and constraints
- Applies to: model swaps, routing changes (tiering/fallback), major prompt/template rewrites, and feature-level LLM behavior changes that touch >0.5% of traffic.
- Excludes: internal infra-only changes with no model/behavior impact.
- Target audience: PM, Eng TL, SRE, Safety Reviewer, Solutions Eng.

Why a calendar-first approach?
- Many rollouts fail because stakeholders miss a short window where a new signal trends bad. Synchronized human checkpoints (fixed times) increase probability of early detection and consistent decisions.
- Creates predictable on-call/observation blocks so engineers can plan deep work around launch windows.

High-level rhythm (example)
- Day -7: Kickoff + risk assessment doc published (owner: PM).
- Day -5: Canary plan + traffic slices and capacity review (owner: Eng TL).
- Day -1: Dress rehearsal in staging + smoke checklist (owner: SRE).
- Launch day 0: 1% exposure at 09:00 local, monitor window 09:00–12:00 (all hands for early-stage), human gate at 12:00. If gate passes, 10% at 13:00, monitor 13:00–18:00, gate at 18:00. If gate passes, scale to target overnight.
- Day +1 and +3: audit pass/fail meeting (safety + PM).

Human gate format (30 min ritual)
- Quick summary (5 min): owner outlines what changed and where traffic is routed.
- Metrics snapshot (10 min): SRE presents latency, error rate, cost delta, model-quality flags (see below).
- Signals from Product/Safety (10 min): qualitative flags, user reports, known false-positive patterns.
- Decision (5 min): proceed, hold, or rollback. Decision logged to confluence + #launches slack.

Gating metrics (stream + point-in-time)
- System: p99 latency, 5xx rate, queue depth, replica restarts. Thresholds: p99 > baseline + 40% -> HARD STOP. 5xx > baseline + 0.5pp -> HARD STOP.
- Cost: tokens per request, cost-per-minute. If cost delta > 3x estimate for sustained 30m -> flag for product review.
- Quality (LLM-specific): regression score on smoke prompt set (rolling evaluation): fail if delta < -0.03 (3 percentage points) for intent-preservation metrics OR hallucination increase > 2x.
- Safety: policy block rate, unsafe-classification delta. Any new safety class >0 -> immediate hold and safety triage.
- User-visible errors: user-facing complaint rate normalized per 10k users. >2x baseline -> escalate.

Traffic slicing rules (example)
- Slice A: internal staff + dogfooders (100% exposure early).
- Slice B: low-risk microcohorts (non-critical paths, <0.1% daily active).
- Slice C: broader customer cohort (by product plan, geography).
- Randomization: for A/B experiments use deterministic hash key _user_id % 10000, assign percent ranges. Store assignment in experiment metadata for audit.

On-call and roles during windows
- Launch Lead (PM): coordinates ritual and final decision.
- Eng TL (owner): rollback, post-mortem author if needed.
- SRE monitor: provides metric snapshots + automations.
- Safety reviewer: triage safety/regression alerts.
- Communications owner: posts gate decisions, external comms if required.
- Backup rota: if primary unavailable, the next person in list is responsible.

Rollback decision matrix (fast path)
- Immediate rollback (within 15m) if: p99 > baseline + 40% OR safety-blocks detected OR 5xx spike.
- Soft-hold (manual throttle) if: cost spikes but no quality loss OR transient latency. Requires product signoff to continue.
- Gradual rollback: scale back to previous model variant (automated via routing policy) and observe for 30m before reattempt.

Observability checklist (minimal)
- Pre-launch: dashboards up (latency/cost/quality/safety), smoke eval harness green in staging, alerting thresholds deployed.
- During: tagging for launch traffic, sample traces for 1% of requests, streaming of sample responses to safety pipeline.
- Post: persistence of sample logs (encrypted) + redaction pass, evaluation artifacts attached to rollout confluence page.

LLM-specific quick measurement recipes
- Smoke-set: 50 prompts covering hallucination, intent, slot extraction. Run before and after change and compute difference.
- Behavioral probes: top-10 prompt families sampled from recent production logs (privacy-safe). Run small-batch eval for drift.
- Latency slicing by seq-length: compare p50/p95/p99 for short (<64 tokens) and long (>512 tokens).

Comms and stakeholder cadence
- T-minus emails: -7d (heads-up), -1d (final plan), immediate (gate result), +24h (summary), +7d (postmortem if any).
- Slack: dedicated channel #launch-<shortname>-YYYYMMDD. Use Slack thread for gate decisions only.

Safety + Privacy considerations
- Sampling for human review: sampled responses must be scrubbed of PII. Use automated PII redactor before human viewing.
- Data retention: sample logs for a rollout kept for 30 days by default unless incident -> 90 days.
- Access: only Safety/Eng/PM have access to full sampled logs during active gate window.

Automation ideas (short list)
- One-button gate: auto-generate gate packet (dashboards + smoke eval snapshot + commit diffs) and a link to click to mark pass/hold/rollback.
- Calendar integration: create calendar blocks for all stakeholders when rollout is scheduled (auto-attach link to channel + confluence page).
- Canary replay harness: if rollback occurs, ability to replay recent requests against new variant in isolated account.

Runbook quick checklist (for on-call)
- Verify tagged dashboards load.
- Confirm model hash/version and routing table match plan.
- Start sampling pipeline and ensure redaction enabled.
- Monitor first 15m for safety blocks and p99 latency.
- Run smoke-set at 30m mark and attach results.

Open questions / TODOs
- What is the precise threshold for hallucination regressions (we have a candidate but need product signoff).
- How to standardize deterministic assignment for multi-device users (cookie vs account id).
- Draft of calendar template for cross-timezone launches (EAST/US/PAC).
- Build minimal "gate packet" generator (engineering spike planned next week).

Notes to self
- Keep rituals short and focused; avoid turning gate calls into long debates. If team can't decide, fallback to rollback.
- Work with Legal on retention policy if sampling hits sensitive customers.

References and links
- existing playbooks: confluence:PROD-ROLLUPS-392 (see rollout checklist section)
- infra tickets: JIRA:INF-8472 (routing automation)
- sample script: github:rollout-scripts/pr-214

End of scratchpad.
